documentation.description:
-
  @summary
  Thin, SPARK-friendly helpers for character and string I/O on a GNAT.Serial_Communications port.

  @description
  Provides simple conversion functions between Stream_Element / Stream_Element_Array and Character / String together
  with the classic Get / Put / Get_Line / Put_Line operations. The package is intended for console-style protocols
  used by classic and modern retro calculators (SwissMicros DM-series, HP-IL emulators, etc.).

documentation.description:
-
  Read a line from the serial port.

  Characters are accumulated until a carriage-return or line-feed is received (the terminator itself is not
  stored). If the buffer is filled before a terminator arrives, Data_Error is raised.

parameters.name: Port
parameters.description:
content from Port, bounds from Text itself

number of characters limited by buffer size
how far the port advanced depends on buffer size

The open serial port.

parameters.name: Text
parameters.description:
content from Port, bounds from Text itself

number of characters limited by buffer size
how far the port advanced depends on buffer size

Buffer that receives the line.

parameters.name: Last
parameters.description:
content from Port, bounds from Text itself

number of characters limited by buffer size
how far the port advanced depends on buffer size

Index of the last character stored in Text (Text'First - 1 if the line was empty).

documentation.description:
-
  Write a string followed by CR+LF to the serial port.

parameters.name: Port
parameters.description:
Mirrors the precondition of To_Stream. A non-null String always has bounds in Positive; the constraint only
excludes null strings whose bounds fall outside Natural, e.g. String (0 .. -1).

The open serial port.

parameters.name: Text
parameters.description:
Mirrors the precondition of To_Stream. A non-null String always has bounds in Positive; the constraint only
excludes null strings whose bounds fall outside Natural, e.g. String (0 .. -1).

The string to transmit (the terminators are added automatically).
